description.narrative: Projektstödet till We Effect i Colombia syftar till att underlätta återintegreringsprocessen för kvinnliga och manliga före-detta soldater tillsammans med deras grannkommuner, genom att genomföra hållbara ekonomiska modeller baserade på kooperativa modeller med ett jämställdhetsperspektiv. Stödet är geografiskt inriktat på Montes de Maria-regionen (Sucre, Bolivar och Cordoba), som alla är konfliktdrabbade regioner. Detta stöd är en andra fas av en tidigare insats för återintegreringsprocessen med ID-nummer: 12204.

The project support to We Effect in Colombia has the objective to facilitate the reincorporation process of female and male ex-combatants jointly with their neighbouring communities, through the implementation of sustainable economic models based on cooperative models with gender perspective included. The contribution has its geographical focus in the Montes de Maria region (Sucre, Bolivar, and Cordoba), which are conflict-affected regions. This contribution is a second phase, building on a previous contribution to the reincorporation process with ID-number: 12204

The proposed impact goal is: Sustainable rural development, resilient to climate change, with gender justice and using cooperative models, which reinforce territorial roots and contribute to the reconstruction of the social fabric and a peaceful society in Colombia."
The outcome goal is men and women ex-combatants in a reincorporation process together with their neighboring communities, implementing sustainable economic models, based on cooperative models and with a gender perspective, guaranteeing access to rights and participation in peace building. The specific objective slightly changed from the concept note, focusing on a specific region. The new proposed specific objective is: men and women ex-combatants in a reincorporation process part of social and solidarity economic organizations from municipalities of the Departments of Bolívar, Sucre and Córdoba, their families and communities participate to improve their socioeconomic conditions and help in building peace.
The following three specific outputs are proposed:
1. The women ex-combatants in a reincorporation process from the organizations and communities of the municipalities of Bolívar, Sucre and Córdoba have strengthened their political and economic empowerment and their capacities to recognize and exercise their rights.
2. Women's and mixed organizations, ex-combatants in a reincorporation process, from the social and solidarity economy in municipalities of Bolívar, Sucre and Córdoba, have comprehensively developed and improved sustainable enterprises leveraged by capital, financial inclusion, knowledge management, associativity, alliances and including the gender approach.
3. Organizations, their families and communities in municipalities in Bolívar, Sucre and Córdoba, particularly women and youth, influence public policies to gain access to rights and help strengthen coexistence and local and regional reconciliation.

- 125 women were graduated in empowerment and prevention of gender-based violence in the strategy Mújeres que Suman, 91% of participants raised their knowledge on these topics.
- Seven gender committees were created in the same number of organizations. Committees promote gender equality, prevention of gender-based violence and support the mainstreaming of gender perspective.
- Eight organizations have received technical assistance and economic support for their sustainability. Economic support was made through the delivery of machinery, consumables, and equipment.
- The board of We Effect visited Colombia in September 2023 and have dialogues with the organizations part of the project and other stakeholders, as a direct result of the visit, We Effect created the Cooperative Business for Development Hub, with the objective to develop strategies to foster partnerships between cooperatives participants in the project and Swedish cooperatives.
- Thirteen partnerships were established for the productive linkage and sustainability of economic initiatives. There are four partnerships to highlight, the first one with AGROSAVIA, for the implementation a new model of cattle farming that is environmentally sustainable. The second one with University of Sucre, for providing technical support for the cooperatives. The third one with Andi Foundation to participate in their marketplace Se le tiene and the last one with Agroexpo Caribe, an event to promote new business relations.
- In collaboration with Bogotá Mayor´s office, was published the book La Ruta TOAR Un camino para la justicia restaurativa en la justicia transicional. The book presents guidelines for the implementation of jobs, works and activities with restorative content (TOAR) that the people included in the different cases handled by the Special Jurisdiction of Peace should do to materialize restoration of the damage caused.
- In September 2023 the government transferred 500 hectares of land to FEDECARIBE in Ovejas, Sucre.
- A campaign to prevent gender-based violence was implemented in the municipalities of Ovejas and Palmitos, involving 169 people. The campaign was named Voces que Transforman, Sentidos que Previenen and was coordinated with the local authorities of the Sucre department and public institutions present in the region.
- 630 former combatants continue their reincorporation process through the participation in the cooperatives that are part of the projects.
- Through a partnership with SENA, three certified training programmes were provided to 35 people to improve their employability.
- With INNPACTIA's support, a mechanism for innovative financing was developed to manage funds from other cooperation actors, such as philanthropic and private sector.
- Coomaria obtained a loan from the Banco Agrario de Colombia. This is a milestone for the project, as it is the first organisation of former combatants to have access to bank credit.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
